goal: Iske baad aap chalte hue program ke memory areas ke naam bata sakte hain, bata sakte hain ke globals, locals aur dynamic data kahan rehte hain, stack frames samjha sakte hain, stack aur heap ka muqabla kar sakte hain, aur stack overflow aur memory leak ko aasaan alfaz mein bayan kar sakte hain.
warmup: Canteen mein plates ek dher mein hoti hain. Aap sirf upar wali plate utha sakte hain aur istemal ki hui plate wapas upar rakh sakte hain: koi isay organise nahi karta, bas yeh chal jata hai, aur bohat tez hai. Yeh stack hai. Heap peeche ke ek bade godown ki tarah hai: aap manager ke paas jate hain, jagah maangte hain, aur khatam hone par wapas karni hoti hai. Agar aap bhool jayein to jagah band rehti hai aur kisi ke kaam nahi aati.
definition: Jab aap ka program chalta hai to computer usay areas mein banti hui memory deta hai. STACK local variables aur function parameters rakhta hai. Yeh automatic hai: function ko call hone par apna block (stack frame) milta hai, aur function ke return hone par block free ho jata hai. Yeh bohat tez hai lekin chhota (kuch MB). HEAP ek bada area hai us memory ke liye jo aap program chalte waqt new operator se maangte hain. Yeh manual hai: aap ko khud delete se wapas karni hoti hai. Global aur static variables teesre area mein rehte hain jo program ke poore run tak maujood rehta hai, aur code khud chauthe mein hota hai.
howItWorks: Pehli trace step by step chalayein. addOne() teen dafa call hota hai. Iska local variable har dafa stack par banta hai aur har call ke aakhir mein khatam ho jata hai, is liye har dafa 1 print hota hai. Static variable kept aur global total stack par NAHI hain: woh poore program tak zinda rehte hain, is liye woh 1, 2, 3 ginte rehte hain. Ab doosri trace kai function calls ko upar neeche rakha hua dikhati hai: main first ko call karta hai, first second ko, second third ko. Call stack panel frames ko jama hote hue aur phir ulti tarteeb mein jaate hue dikhata hai: jo frame sab se aakhir mein aaya woh sab se pehle jata hai. Kyunke har function ka apna frame hota hai, har ek ke apne variables (a, b, c) hote hain jo doosre nahi dekh sakte. Teesri misaal mein (aur memory visual mein) ek value ki zaroorat us function ke khatam hone ke BAAD hoti hai jis ne usay banaya. Aam local return ke zariye bahar copy ho jata hai, jo chhoti values ke liye theek hai. Bade data ke liye ya us data ke liye jo zyada der zinda rehna chahiye, program heap se new int ke zariye box maang sakta hai. Pointer p stack par local variable hai aur gayab ho jata hai, lekin heap ka box tab tak rehta hai jab tak aap delete na karein. Abhi new aur delete ki fikar na karein: agla lesson unhein theek se sikhata hai. Do mashhoor masle: STACK OVERFLOW tab hota hai jab stack bhar jaye, masalan aisa function jo khud ko hamesha call karta rahe (infinite recursion) ya bohat bada local array; program crash ho jata hai. MEMORY LEAK tab hota hai jab aap heap memory lein aur kabhi wapas na karein; program aahista aahista zyada se zyada memory khata jata hai. Hum yeh dono lesson mein kabhi nahi chalate, kyunke yeh bugs hain.
